author: orchestrator
summary: research a router LLM that decides whether to call Haiku, Sonnet, or Opus based on query complexity. Build something that goes beyond what is already existing and outperforms the baselines that already exist.
seed: research a router LLM that decides whether to call Haiku, Sonnet, or Opus based on query complexity. Build something that goes beyond what is already existing and outperforms the baselines that already exist.

author: idea-expander
summary: Multi-signal feature router (token count + lexical diversity + syntactic depth + task-type embedding) achieves ≥85% routing accuracy, beating length-only heuristics.
claim: A lightweight ternary classifier trained on rich query features—token count, type-token ratio, avg parse-tree depth, and 4-way task-type label—routes queries to the cheapest tier that can answer them without >2% quality loss compared to always using Opus, achieving ≥85% routing accuracy on MMLU+GSM8K+HumanEval.

author: idea-expander
summary: Confidence-cascade routing (cheap-model-first, escalate on low confidence) achieves cost-normalized quality ≥15% better than a flat upfront router on diverse benchmarks.
claim: A cascading system that first routes all queries to Haiku, escalates to Sonnet if Haiku self-reported token-probability confidence < τ₁, and escalates to Opus if Sonnet confidence < τ₂, achieves cost_normalized_quality ≥ 1.15× compared to a flat upfront multi-signal router, on MMLU+GSM8K+HumanEval.

author: idea-expander
summary: [CROSS-DOMAIN TRANSPLANT from adaptive bitrate streaming] BOLA-inspired online-adaptive router limits quality degradation to <3% within 50 queries after an abrupt domain shift.
claim: Adapting the BOLA ABR streaming algorithm to LLM routing—replacing buffer-occupancy with a rolling quality-cost balance score—re-calibrates tier thresholds within 50 queries after an abrupt domain shift, keeping mean quality within 3% of a clairvoyant oracle router that knows the new domain in advance.

author: idea-expander
summary: Self-supervised routing via output-entropy labeling closes within 5pp routing accuracy of fully-supervised routing, eliminating costly human-labeled difficulty annotation.
claim: A router trained on self-supervised difficulty labels—where each query's label is derived from the entropy of k=5 sampled Haiku completions (high entropy = hard, low entropy = easy)—achieves routing_accuracy within 0.05 absolute points of a supervised router trained on human-annotated difficulty labels, on MMLU+GSM8K+HumanEval.

author: literature-scout
summary: Kadavath et al. (Anthropic) show output entropy H(A|Q) over sampled completions discriminates questions a model answers correctly from those it fails—directly validating HYP-004's entropy-labeling mechanism, but with an important caveat: AUROC trend is negative on HumanEval as models scale.
title: Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know
key_claims: Output entropy H(A|Q) estimated from N=200 samples at T=1 has predictive power for whether a model answers correctly (AUROC 0.7–0.87 on TriviaQA/HumanEval for 52B model).

Larger models produce more diverse *correct* answers on code tasks (HumanEval), causing a *negative* AUROC trend for entropy-based difficulty detection as model size grows—conflating answer diversity with difficulty.
P(IK) trained with soft labels derived from fraction-correct across 30 samples achieves strong in-distribution AUROC (0.86 on TriviaQA) and partial cross-task generalization.
Showing a model many of its own T=1 samples before asking P(True) significantly improves self-evaluation—the k-sample brainstorming protocol is analogous to HYP-004's k=5 sampling plan.
Token-level entropy must be length-normalized to avoid confounding by response length, especially for open-ended tasks.

author: literature-scout
summary: Kuhn et al. (Oxford) introduce Semantic Entropy—entropy over clustered meanings rather than raw token sequences—which outperforms raw entropy for predicting LLM accuracy on QA, directly bearing on HYP-004's token-level entropy labeling quality.
title: Semantic Uncertainty: Linguistic Invariances for Uncertainty Estimation in Natural Language Generation
key_claims: Raw token-level entropy is a biased uncertainty measure because semantically equivalent answers (e.g., "Paris is the capital" vs. "The capital is Paris") inflate apparent entropy without reflecting genuine model uncertainty.

Semantic entropy—clustering sampled outputs by bi-directional NLI entailment, then computing entropy over meaning clusters—is more predictive of model accuracy than raw entropy or P(True) baselines (Kadavath et al. 2022).
Semantic entropy scales better with model size and number of samples than raw entropy; it is fully unsupervised and requires no labels or finetuning.
On TriviaQA with a 30B OPT model, semantic entropy achieves higher AUROC than normalized entropy, lexical similarity, and P(True) baselines.
The method requires only black-box sampling from a single model and a lightweight NLI classifier—compatible with API-only access to Haiku.

author: literature-scout
summary: Wang et al. (Google) show that sampling diverse reasoning paths and taking majority vote (self-consistency) robustly improves CoT accuracy—the consistency/agreement signal across samples is an unsupervised, label-free proxy for difficulty that underpins HYP-004's entropy approach.
title: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models
key_claims: Sampling k diverse reasoning paths at T>0 and marginalizing via majority vote consistently outperforms greedy CoT decoding across arithmetic and commonsense benchmarks (+17.9% on GSM8K).
Correct reasoning processes, even when diverse in form, tend to converge on the same final answer; incorrect paths diverge—implying that answer *agreement* is an implicit difficulty signal.
Self-consistency is entirely unsupervised, requires no extra training, and works off-the-shelf from a single pretrained LLM—establishing the feasibility of label-free quality signals from sampling.
Performance gains hold across model scales (UL2-20B to PaLM-540B) and are robust to sampling temperature and imperfect prompts.
The method is orthogonal to routing: it improves per-query accuracy but does not decide which model to route to—the routing decision remains external.

author: literature-scout
summary: BOLA uses Lyapunov optimization for near-optimal adaptive bitrate streaming, the direct algorithmic source for HYP-003.
title: BOLA: Near-Optimal Bitrate Adaptation for Online Videos
key_claims: BOLA formulates ABR as utility-maximization and solves it with Lyapunov drift-plus-penalty, achieving time-average utility within O(1/V) of optimal.
BOLA requires no bandwidth prediction; reacts to observed buffer occupancy, making it robust to abrupt throughput changes.
Control parameter V trades buffer stability vs. video quality, directly analogous to budget-quality tradeoff V in HYP-003.
Deployed in production by Akamai, BBC, CBS, and Orange validating industrial viability.

author: literature-scout
summary: FrugalGPT shows LLM cascade cuts cost 98% via static trained thresholds, but requires same-distribution training data — vulnerable to domain shift.
title: FrugalGPT: How to Use Large Language Models While Reducing Cost and Improving Performance
key_claims: LLM cascade with learned scoring thresholds reduces cost up to 98% while matching GPT-4 accuracy on fixed-distribution benchmarks.
Requires labeled examples from same or similar distribution as test data; distribution shift breaks the cascade strategy.
Routing decisions made via a static DistilBERT scoring function trained offline — no online adaptation mechanism.
Three cost-reduction strategies: prompt adaptation, LLM approximation, LLM cascade.

author: literature-scout
summary: Chen et al. (Stanford) propose FrugalGPT—an LLM cascade that uses a learned generation-scoring function to decide when to escalate from cheap to expensive models—providing a cost-reduction baseline and the generation-scoring primitive that HYP-004's entropy labeler would replace.
title: FrugalGPT: How to Use Large Language Models While Reducing Cost and Improving Performance
key_claims: FrugalGPT can match GPT-4 performance with up to 98% cost reduction, or improve accuracy by 4% at equal cost, by learning which LLM combinations to use per query.
The generation scoring function g(q, a) is the central routing primitive—it assesses response reliability post-hoc and triggers escalation; it is learned from labeled correctness data.
LLM cascade requires labeled training data for the scoring function: ground-truth correctness of cheap-model answers must be known at training time, making it a supervised approach.
Heterogeneous LLM pricing (up to 100x differences) motivates query-adaptive routing—the cost savings from routing even 50% of queries to Haiku are substantial.
FrugalGPT is evaluated on HEADLINES, MedQA, and Open Assistant—diverse domains—showing that routing generalizes across task types when the scoring function is sufficiently expressive.

author: literature-scout
summary: Hybrid LLM proposes quality-gap-aware router achieving 40% fewer large-model calls; routing threshold is fixed post-training with no online adaptation.
title: Hybrid LLM: Cost-Efficient and Quality-Aware Query Routing
key_claims: Router trained to predict quality gap between small and large models; routes to small model if predicted gap below tunable threshold.
Achieves up to 40% fewer large-model calls with <1% quality drop on held-out in-distribution test sets.
Quality threshold is tunable at test time but requires manual selection — not automatic adaptation.
No cross-domain or domain-shift evaluation performed.

author: literature-scout
summary: RouteLLM trains preference-data-based routers achieving >2x cost savings with strong OOD generalization, but all training is offline with no online adaptation.
title: RouteLLM: Learning to Route LLMs with Preference Data
key_claims: Framework trains router models from human preference data achieving over 2x cost reduction without quality loss.
Routers generalize to unseen LLM pairs without retraining, showing cross-model transferability.
Evaluates BERT classifier, matrix factorization, and SW-ranking router architectures.
No online adaptation mechanism; all routers are trained offline on a fixed preference dataset.

author: literature-scout
summary: Ong et al. (UC Berkeley/Anyscale) introduce RouteLLM—a framework for learning routers from human preference data that achieves >2x cost savings with minimal quality loss—establishing the state-of-the-art supervised routing baseline that HYP-004's self-supervised approach aims to match within 5pp.
title: RouteLLM: Learning to Route LLMs with Preference Data
key_claims: Routers trained on Chatbot Arena human preference data achieve >2x cost reduction while maintaining response quality comparable to GPT-4 on MMLU and MT-Bench.
Data augmentation techniques (e.g., generating synthetic preference labels) significantly improve routing performance across all router architectures tested.
Routers generalize to LLM pairs not seen during training, suggesting that routing signals capture query complexity properties independent of specific model pair.
The key supervised signal is pairwise human preference (strong vs. weak model win/loss/tie)—expensive to collect but highly informative.
Router training from only ~10K preference examples is sufficient for strong performance, suggesting sample efficiency of the supervision signal.

author: literature-scout
summary: LLM-Blender shows no single LLM dominates (best wins only 21% of cases), motivating adaptive per-query tier selection across domain shifts.
title: LLM-Blender: Ensembling Large Language Models with Pairwise Ranking and Generative Fusion
key_claims: No single open-source LLM dominates: top-1 LLM wins only 21% of examples on MixInstruct benchmark.
PairRanker using cross-attention pairwise comparisons outperforms point-wise scoring for subtle quality differences.
GenFuser achieves average rank 3.2 vs. best individual LLM rank 3.9 on MixInstruct.
Method requires querying all N LLMs per input — too expensive for production routing, motivating single-model routing over ensembling.

author: literature-scout
summary: FrugalGPT introduces LLM cascade with learned scoring function: matches GPT-4 accuracy with 98% cost reduction.
title: FrugalGPT: How to Use Large Language Models While Reducing Cost and Improving Performance
key_claims: LLM cascade stops when g(q,a) exceeds per-LLM threshold
98% cost reduction matching GPT-4 on HEADLINES
Scorer trained on (query,answer) pairs—not token log-probs
Cascade beats single-model baseline when cheapest model handles >70% queries

author: literature-scout
summary: RouteLLM learns preference-data-based routers, reducing cost >2x at parity quality; single-query design avoids cascade latency.
title: RouteLLM: Learning to Route LLMs with Preference Data
key_claims: Upfront routing from Chatbot Arena preference data reduces cost >2x on MMLU/MT-Bench without quality loss
Win-probability model P(win_strong|q) trained via cross-entropy; threshold α controls cost-quality tradeoff
Routers generalize to unseen LLM pairs (strong transfer learning)
Single-query design explicitly avoids cascade latency—key raised as advantage over FrugalGPT

author: literature-scout
summary: CALM uses calibrated per-token confidence for early exit in LLMs, achieving 3x speedup with provable sequence-level quality guarantees.
title: Confident Adaptive Language Modeling
key_claims: Per-token softmax entropy at intermediate layer calibrated via distribution-free risk control (LTT) to satisfy global sequence-level quality bounds
3x speedup on summarization, MT, QA with provably bounded quality degradation
Token-level confidence saturation events motivate using intermediate representations as confidence proxy
LTT framework connects local exit decisions to global constraints without labeled data

author: literature-scout
summary: Kadavath et al. (Anthropic) show large LMs are well-calibrated on MC/T-F; P(True) self-evaluation distinguishes correct from incorrect samples.
title: Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know
key_claims: Large LMs (52B) are well-calibrated on diverse MC/T-F questions in correct format; calibration improves with model size
P(True) self-evaluation reliably distinguishes correct from incorrect open-ended samples
P(IK) trained to predict model self-knowledge generalizes partially across task domains
RLHF-tuned models appear miscalibrated but temperature scaling restores calibration

author: literature-scout
summary: Self-Consistency: sampling diverse CoT paths + majority vote boosts GSM8K by +17.9%; answer agreement across paths is a calibration-free confidence proxy.
title: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models
key_claims: Sample-and-marginalize over k reasoning paths improves GSM8K by 17.9%, SVAMP by 11%, AQuA by 12.2%
Answer consistency across sampled paths correlates strongly with correctness—a sampling-based confidence proxy
Unsupervised: no additional training, auxiliary models, or fine-tuning required
Works across 4 model scales (UL2-20B, GPT-3, LaMDA-137B, PaLM-540B)

author: literature-scout
summary: Speculative decoding: cheap draft model + expensive target model for 2-3x speedup; token acceptance rate is structurally analogous to cascade escalation rate.
title: Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding
key_claims: Small draft model generates γ speculative tokens; large target model accepts/rejects in parallel via speculative sampling
2-3x wall-time speedup on T5-XXL with identical output distribution
Token acceptance rate depends on draft-target KL divergence: easy tokens accepted at high rates, hard tokens rejected
Training-free and architecture-agnostic

author: literature-scout
summary: FrugalGPT: LLM cascade achieves 98% cost reduction via output-conditional scoring; pre-generation query-feature routing is unexplored.
title: FrugalGPT: How to Use Large Language Models While Reducing Cost and Improving Performance
key_claims: LLM cascade with learned DistilBERT scoring achieves 98% cost reduction vs. GPT-4 on HEADLINES.
Scoring function g(q,a) is output-conditional -- requires at least one model call before routing.
No evaluation of pre-generation query-feature-only routing (token count, TTR, parse depth, task type).
Cost variation across LLM APIs is up to 2 orders of magnitude, motivating routing.
Three cost-reduction strategies: prompt adaptation, LLM approximation, LLM cascade.

author: literature-scout
summary: RouteLLM: BERT router trained on human preference data achieves >2x cost savings on MMLU/MT-Bench; uses dense embeddings not interpretable features.
title: RouteLLM: Learning to Route LLMs with Preference Data
key_claims: Win-prediction classifier on Chatbot Arena preference labels achieves >2x cost savings on MMLU/MT-Bench without quality loss.
Data augmentation of preference labels significantly boosts performance across all architectures.
Routers generalize to unseen LLM pairs, suggesting routing signal is intrinsic to query complexity.
Binary routing only; ternary/N-way routing noted as future work.
Router uses raw BERT embeddings -- no interpretable syntactic or lexical features; ~20ms CPU latency.

author: literature-scout
summary: Hybrid LLM: DeBERTa quality-gap router achieves 40% fewer large-model calls at <1% quality drop; most architecturally similar prior work to HYP-001.
title: Hybrid LLM: Cost-Efficient and Quality-Aware Query Routing
key_claims: DeBERTa encoder trained on soft quality-gap labels (10 samples per query) routes binary, achieving 40% fewer large-model calls at <1% BART-score drop.
Soft labels (probability that small model quality >= large model quality) outperform hard labels.
Data transformation improves routing when the capability gap between models is very large.
Router overhead is negligible (single encoder forward pass) vs. autoregressive decoding.
No syntactic features used; routing relies on DeBERTa contextual embeddings; binary routing only.

author: literature-scout
summary: AutoMix: POMDP router using few-shot self-verification achieves >50% cost reduction; output-conditional cascade contrasting with HYP-001 pre-generation approach.
title: AutoMix: Automatically Mixing Language Models
key_claims: POMDP router using small-model self-verification (entailment check) achieves >50% cost reduction on 5 context-grounded QA datasets.
Self-verification framed as NLI entailment; probability estimated from k samples at high temperature.
Router learns from as few as 50 training examples.
POMDP handles noisy verification by maintaining a belief over query difficulty states.
Requires one small-model call + verification per query -- not a zero-call pre-generation approach.

author: literature-scout
summary: RouterBench: First standardized routing benchmark with 405k inference outcomes across 11 LLMs/8 datasets; validates simple supervised classifiers are competitive.
title: RouterBench: A Benchmark for Multi-LLM Routing System
key_claims: RouterBench provides 405k pre-computed inference outcomes from 11 LLMs across 8 diverse datasets for router evaluation without re-running inference.
Predictive routing (pre-generation classifier) distinguished from non-predictive routing (cascade) in formal taxonomy.
Simple supervised classifiers already outperform many baselines, validating lightweight pre-generation approaches.
Monetary costs vary 2-5x across LLMs for comparable performance, motivating routing.
No feature ablation study -- the benchmark supports any routing method but does not identify which query features matter.

author: literature-scout
summary: LLM-Blender: PairRanker shows best LLM wins only 21% of examples, empirically motivating per-query routing; ensemble approach calls all N models unlike HYP-001.
title: LLM-Blender: Ensembling Large Language Models with Pairwise Ranking and Generative Fusion
key_claims: No single LLM dominates: best model (Vicuna) ranks first on only 21% of examples, showing high per-query variability in optimal model choice.
PairRanker (cross-attention RoBERTa) using pairwise output comparison outperforms pointwise ranking.
LLM-Blender achieves average rank 3.2 vs. best individual model rank 3.9 on MixInstruct.
MixInstruct benchmark (100k train / 5k test) with oracle pairwise comparisons is a usable training resource.
Requires N model calls to generate candidates -- not cost-efficient; contrasts with HYP-001 single pre-generation routing call.

author: idea-expander
summary: Latency-SLA-aware router that incorporates EWMA latency estimates per tier reduces P95 latency ≥25% vs. cost-only router at matched mean quality.
claim: A router augmented with a per-tier EWMA of observed API response times, which overrides the cost-optimal tier when predicted P95 latency would breach a configurable SLA threshold, reduces measured P95 latency by ≥25% relative to a cost-only RouteLLM-style router on an interactive mixed-domain query set, while maintaining mean quality within 2% of the cost-only router.

author: idea-expander
summary: Conversation-aware router conditioning on dialogue complexity trajectory reduces unnecessary Opus escalations ≥20% vs. per-query router on MT-Bench without quality loss.
claim: A router encoding the rolling complexity trajectory of a multi-turn dialogue—mean cosine distance between successive turn embeddings and entropy of the running topic distribution over the last k=5 turns—reduces unnecessary escalations to Opus by ≥20% compared to a per-query-only router, while maintaining LLM-judge quality within 2% on MT-Bench multi-turn conversations.

author: critic
summary: EWMA latency tracking is engineering-focused; core novelty is incremental.
concerns: EWMA is a standard technique applied straightforwardly to model latencies
Latency-SLA enforcement is production-critical but not scientifically novel
Hypothesis orthogonal to core routing research (cost-quality tradeoff)
Mechanism is engineering-sound but lacks algorithmic depth
proposed_fix: Continue if project prioritizes production-readiness; park if focus is algorithmic novelty. Strengthen by proposing joint latency-cost-quality optimization (e.g., Lagrangian relaxation or Pareto frontier estimation).

author: critic
summary: HYP-002 applies established cascading + confidence calibration without algorithmic novelty; high boredom, candidate for parking.
concerns: token log-prob confidence is textbook technique
mechanism is straightforward thresholding without algorithmic insight
predicted gains (15%) are modest vs. FrugalGPT baseline (98%)
comparison scope limited to HYP-001, not SOTA methods
proposed_fix: Park HYP-002 or deprioritize in favor of HYP-003/HYP-004 which offer clearer conceptual novelty.

author: critic
summary: HYP-003 mechanically straightforward cross-domain transplant; online-adaptation novelty offset by trivial variable substitution and narrow prediction scope
concerns: BOLA→LLM mapping is obvious once stated: buffer→QCBS, bandwidth→domain-difficulty; Lyapunov optimization unchanged from original
50-query convergence claim is narrow; only tests abrupt shifts, not steady-state or gradual domain drift—generalization unclear
Quality estimation via 10% sampled judge introduces latency/cost overhead; feasibility to stay within production SLAs (<100ms/routing decision) unvetted
proposed_fix: Parallel validation: (1) empirically confirm <3% degradation vs. static baseline post-shift, (2) profile end-to-end latency including judge sampling—failure on either breaks the hypothesis novelty claim

author: critic
summary: HYP-001 is redundant with Hybrid LLM; no novel mechanism or feature signal
concerns: LIT-019 (Hybrid LLM) is architecturally identical—both use a learned classifier to route to Haiku/Sonnet/Opus tiers. The only difference is the feature set (parse depth + TTR), which is marginal engineering, not novelty.
Hand-crafted features are a dead-end. LIT-008/LIT-009 (RouteLLM) uses learned BERT embeddings and achieves >2x cost savings with strong OOD generalization.
Achieves 85% routing accuracy, but Hybrid LLM already gets 40% fewer large-model calls with <1% quality loss (LIT-007/LIT-019). Not a meaningful improvement.

No online adaptation, self-supervised learning, or novel mechanism. Unlike HYP-003 (BOLA), HYP-004 (entropy), HYP-005 (latency-aware), this is purely offline supervised classification—the frontier moved past this.
RouterBench (LIT-021) shows simple classifiers are already competitive. Building another supervised classifier adds no novelty.
proposed_fix: Park HYP-001 and focus on mechanistically novel hypotheses: online adaptation (HYP-003), self-supervised learning (HYP-004), latency/SLA awareness (HYP-005), conversation context (HYP-006).

author: critic
summary: HYP-006 feature-engineering incremental on narrow benchmark; statistical power insufficient
concerns: Incremental feature engineering (HYP-001 + dialogue features); narrow single-benchmark evaluation (MT-Bench only, n=80 conversations); circular baseline dependency; unclear practical impact; small test set undermines statistical power for 20% threshold; conversation context for routing is expected, not surprising
proposed_fix: Either defer until validated on ≥2 additional multi-turn benchmarks, OR reframe to isolate when conversation context specifically helps (e.g., trajectory entropy predicts cascade failure on reasoning tasks)

author: experiment-designer
summary: Conversation-aware vs per-query LightGBM router on MT-Bench multi-turn: measure unnecessary escalation reduction with bootstrap CI
dataset: MT-Bench (80 multi-turn conversations, 640 turn-level decisions; synthetic augmentation to 200 conversations via turn-order shuffling for robustness check)

baseline_spec.model: LightGBM per-query router (HYP-001 feature set: token_count, lexical_diversity, syntactic_depth, task_type_embedding)
baseline_spec.budget: same train/test split and compute envelope as proposed router

steps: 1. Load MT-Bench multi-turn dataset (80 conversations). Generate oracle labels: for each turn, determine cheapest tier (Haiku/Sonnet/Opus) achieving quality within 2% of Opus via cached LLM-judge scores.

2. Feature extraction: (a) Per-query features (baseline): token_count, lexical_diversity (type-token ratio), syntactic_depth (spaCy parse tree height), task_type_embedding (8-dim softmax over topic prototypes). (b) Conversation features (proposed): embed each turn with all-MiniLM-L6-v2; compute trajectory_drift (mean pairwise cosine distance over k=5 turn window), topic_entropy (entropy over 8-topic prototype similarities), turn_index, is_followup_flag (cosine_sim(q_t, q_{t-1}) > 0.7).
3. Train/test split: 60/20 conversations (stratified by first-turn category). Freeze split before any training.
4. Train baseline LightGBM on per-query features only (train set turns). Train proposed LightGBM on per-query + conversation features (same train set turns, same hyperparams).

5. Evaluate on test set: (a) For each test turn, record both routers tier predictions. (b) unnecessary_escalation_reduction_ratio = 1 - (proposed_unnecessary_escalations / baseline_unnecessary_escalations), where unnecessary_escalation = router chose higher tier than oracle. (c) mean_quality_delta = mean(proposed_quality - baseline_quality) using oracle tier quality scores.
6. Bootstrap: resample test conversations (not turns) 1000 times, compute metric distribution and 95% CI. Report pass if CI lower bound > 0 and point estimate >= 0.20.
7. Repeat steps 3-6 for each seed (controls train/test split shuffle and LightGBM random_state).

author: experiment-designer
summary: Self-supervised entropy-router vs supervised router on synthetic MMLU+GSM8K+HumanEval proxy (LightGBM, 3 seeds, baseline=supervised labels)
